note: Curated 2026-10-02 for #5653 (Decoding the Maya Script). Milestones from Coe, Breaking the Maya Code (chapter 'Forefathers: the dawn of decipherment') and Wikipedia 'Maya script' > Decipherment, matched to open IA scans. Already held, not re-imported: Landa Relación (Brasseur 1864, 2 copies), Brasseur Manuscrit Troano (2 vols), Rosny Codex Cortesianus, Dresden (2) and Paris codices, Förstemann 1906 Commentary, Brinton Critical Remarks + Maya Chronicles, Stephens Incidents (hidden), Maudslay Biologia Centrali-Americana (hidden). NOT found as an open scan: Rosny, Essai sur le déchiffrement de l'écriture hiératique (1876) - not on IA or Gallica; HathiTrust is behind a Cloudflare challenge from this box. Rosny's 1878 Revue orientale offprint on the same thesis is imported instead. Gates's Landa (1937) exists only as the 1978 Dover reprint under controlled lending, so it is not imported. In copyright and not imported: Whorf 1933+, Thompson 1950/1962, Knorozov 1952, Berlin 1958, Proskouriakoff 1960, Coe 1992.

BOOKS.title: Proceedings of the American Antiquarian Society, 1878-1880 (with Valentini, 'The Landa Alphabet; a Spanish Fabrication')
BOOKS.author: American Antiquarian Society; Philipp J. J. Valentini
BOOKS.note: Bound run of the old-series Proceedings. Holds Valentini's April 1880 paper arguing Landa's alphabet was a Spanish invention (djvu text: 'THE LANDA ALPHABET; A SPANISH FABRICATION'), and his 'Katunes of Maya History' (Oct 1879).

BOOKS.note: Offprint from the Revue orientale et américaine; stands in for Rosny's 1876 Essai sur le déchiffrement, which has no open scan we can reach. Copy has six inserted hand-written pages of a German translation.
